text:
anya: Heads up — seeing a ~5% bump in p99 on prod for long-sequence tenants in the last hour. pprof snapshot: https://pprof.internal/redwood/2187654321 (root span shows extra 200-400ms waiting in batch queue after KV miss -> mini-batch ejection).
perf-bot: alert: serving-regression detected (p99 +5%). trigger: batcher_eject_rate spike.
sam: I can reproduce in staging with seq_len=1024 and mixed KV hit/miss pattern. behavior: batcher abandons an accumulating batch when one request hits a KV miss, ejects subset, then long requests get deprioritized.
jake: can you paste the trace snippet or the small pprof flame? also what's our current `token_budget_target` and `min_batch_tokens` for that pool?
anya: snippet below (trimmed):
```
batcher_wait_ms  -> 260
kv_lookup_ms     -> 18
eject_path_ms    -> 80
kernel_exec_ms   -> 120
```
current config (canary pool):
```
max_batch_delay_ms: 10
min_batch_tokens: 8
token_budget_target: 64
batch_eject_threshold: 0.35
```
mari: Sounds like token_budget_target is too aggressive for long lanes. When an in-flight KV miss causes partial ejection, the remaining long requests fall below min_batch_tokens and get queued behind short sequences. My quick idea: introduce `reserved_tokens_for_long_lane` or lane weighting so long lanes keep a small reserve to avoid starvation.
riley: we tried pure lane_weights last quarter; it reduced starvation but introduced oscillation under variable load. A smoothing rule on weight updates helps. Example: `weight_long = 0.85*weight_long_old + 0.15*observed_priority` — slow updates to avoid flip-flopping.
sam: Also consider limiting `batch_eject_rate` (max fraction of a batch that can be ejected per unit time) and falling back to a streaming-friendly kernel for long sequences when KV miss frequency spikes. That minimizes the penalty of partial batch breakdowns.
jake: Proposed quick plan: 1) Canary change: add `long_lane_reserve: 32` (reserve 32 tokens per long lane) and clamp `token_budget_target` for long lanes to `token_budget_target + reserve`. 2) Add two telemetry metrics: `batch_eject_rate_per_lane` and `avg_wait_ms_per_lane`. 3) Run 2h canary on dedicated canary pool and compare p99 for long tenants. @mari @riley ok?
mari: :thumbsup: I'll add Grafana panels for the two metrics and a simple alert if avg_wait_ms_long > 150ms.
riley: I'll draft the smoothing + config flag `long_lane_reserve` and add unit tests around ejection accounting. Pseudoconfig: 
```
queue_policy:
  max_batch_delay_ms: 10
  min_batch_tokens: 8
  token_budget_target: 64
  long_lane_reserve: 32
  lane_weight_smoothing_alpha: 0.15
  max_batch_eject_fraction_per_sec: 0.2
```
anya: Owners: jake -> run canary and compare traces, riley -> implement smoothing + reserve flag + tests, mari -> dashboards/alerts. Target: 48h to validate and promote if good.
infra-bot: Canary scheduled: pool=canary-dedicated-3 start_ts=2187655000.
jake: I'll also add a microbenchmark that toggles KV hit/miss at 30% to ensure we don't regress throughput. Will post results in this thread.
anya: Thanks — if canary looks clean, we can roll to a small subset of production tenants next window. Keeping this thread for traces and numbers.
